prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1162; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: At the scene in Pasadena, Texas, I found a low-speed head-on collision between two passenger vehicles. Driver 1 was traveling in the northbound lane when the front of the vehicle struck the front of Driver 2's vehicle as Driver 2 attempted to pull into the lane. Both vehicles sustained front-end damage consistent with the impact described by the drivers. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and was evaluated at the scene. A Passenger was also seated in Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed by officers and independent witnesses to have been present during the crash. Several witnesses on the sidewalk described the collision as I have recorded it, and photographs taken at the scene match these accounts. Driver 2 confirmed the sequence of events. A few small scratches on the rear bumper of Driver 1's vehicle may predate this incident and have been noted separately. Driver 1 stated they reside in the same household as the registered policyholder of the vehicle.
